Clinical Treamtent Summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of
neck and back strain. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported soft
tissue findings, and the force of the impact is in keeping with this type of strain. No
prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions is known from the patient's history or
available records.
Over the course of care, the patient attended 32 visits. Treatment expanded over
successive months, with additional services added beyond what is typically required
for a strain of this kind. Imaging of the cervical and lumbar spine was unremarkable.
During the clinical course, the patient was observed moving freely outside the
examination room, which did not align with the restriction described during formal
assessment. Billing records reviewed for this episode show no repeated charges for the
same service.
Recommendation: Continue monitoring. Reassess functional limits at the next scheduled
visit and consider a formal capacity evaluation if complaints persist.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
